title_en: Order Granting Conditional Exemptive Relief Relating to Certain Centrally Cleared U.S. Treasury Transactions
title_ja: SECの中央清算される一部の米国債取引の証拠金に関する条件付き免除命令
original_text:
SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION

[Release No. 34-106821; File No. S7-2026-26]

Order Under Section 36 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Exchange Act”)

Granting Conditional Exemptive Relief from Section 15(c)(3) of and Rule 15c3-3a, Note H

under the Exchange Act Relating to Certain Centrally Cleared U.S. Treasury Transactions

November 4, 2026.

I.     Introduction

       A.       Overview of Exemptive Order

       The Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) is granting exemptive relief

to broker-dealers from certain provisions of Note H to Item 15 of Exhibit A to Exchange Act

Rule 15c3-3 (“Rule 15c3-3a, Note H” or “Note H”) pursuant to section 36 1 of the Exchange Act.

More specifically, the Commission is granting exemptive relief from the application of Exchange

Act section 15(c)(3) 2 and Rule 15c3-3a, Note H(b)(1) and (b)(2)(i) thereunder to permit broker-

dealers to include a debit in their Rule 15c3-3a customer and proprietary securities accounts of

other broker-dealers (“PAB”) 3 reserve computations (collectively “reserve computations”) for

margin required and on deposit with a qualified clearing agency 4 resulting from transactions in

U.S. Treasury securities in customer accounts that have been cleared, settled, and novated by the


1
       15 U.S.C. 78mm. Section 36(a)(1) of the Exchange Act gives the Commission the authority to exempt any
       person, security or transaction or any class or classes of persons, securities or transactions, conditionally or
       unconditionally, from any Exchange Act provision by rule, regulation or order, to the extent that the
       exemption is necessary or appropriate in the public interest and consistent with the protection of investors.
2
       15 U.S.C. 78o(c)(3).
3

       (which includes a foreign broker-dealer, or a foreign bank acting as a broker-dealer) other than a delivery-
       versus-payment account or a receipt-versus-payment account. The term does not include an account that
       has been subordinated to the claims of creditors of the carrying broker-dealer.)
4

       under section 17A of the Exchange Act that clears, settles, and novates transactions in U.S. Treasury
       securities).

clearing agency in cases where the qualified clearing agency has calculated customer margin on

either a net, omnibus or gross, customer-by-customer basis, and the broker-dealer has delivered

the margin collateral on a net, omnibus basis. 5

       B.      Background

       Rule 15c3-3 under the Exchange Act, the broker-dealer customer protection rule, requires

broker-dealers that hold customer cash and securities (“carrying broker-dealers”) to treat these

assets in a manner that facilitates their prompt return to the customers if the broker-dealer fails

financially. To meet this objective, Rule 15c3-3 requires a carrying broker-dealer to take two

primary steps to safeguard customer assets, which are designed to protect customers by

segregating their securities and cash from the carrying broker-dealer’s proprietary business

activities. The first step requires carrying broker-dealers to maintain physical possession or

control over customers’ fully paid and excess margin securities. 6 The second step requires that a

carrying broker-dealer maintain a reserve of cash or qualified securities (e.g., U.S. Treasury

securities) in an account at a third-party bank that is at least equal in value to the net cash owed

to customers determined by a computation pursuant to a formula set forth in Exchange Act Rule

15c3-3a, the customer reserve computation. 7 The goal of Rule 15c3-3 is to place a broker-dealer

in a position where it is able to wind down and return customer assets in an orderly self-

liquidation without the need for financial assistance.

       On December 13, 2023, the Commission adopted rules under the Exchange Act to amend

the standards applicable to certain clearing agencies to enhance risk management practices for



5
       See Note H(b)(2)(i) to Exhibit A to Rule 15c3-3, 17 CFR 240.15c3-3a.
6
       See 17 CFR 240.15c3-3(d).
7
       See 17 CFR 240.15c3-3a (Formula for determination of customer and PAB account reserve requirements of
       broker-dealers under 17 CFR 240.15c3-3.).

                                                     2

central counterparties in the U.S. Treasury market and facilitate additional clearing of U.S.

Treasury securities. 8 In the Treasury Clearing Adopting Release, the Commission adopted

amendments to Rule 15c3-3a to permit margin required and on deposit at qualified clearing

agencies providing central counterparty services for U.S. Treasury securities to be included by

broker-dealers as a debit in the reserve computations, subject to certain conditions. 9

                i. Gross vs. Net Customer Position Margin Requirement

       Among the conditions necessary for including customer position margin as a debit in the

reserve computations is that customer position margin must be treated in accordance with rules

that must be adopted by the qualified clearing agency. 10 Paragraph (b)(2)(i) of Note H requires

the qualified clearing agency to calculate a separate margin amount for each customer of the

broker-dealer on a gross basis, and requires the broker-dealer to deliver that amount of margin

for each customer on a gross, customer-by-customer basis. 11 The Commission adopted this

requirement to ensure that the risk of one customer’s positions could not be offset by the risk of

another customer’s positions in determining the amount of customer margin the broker-dealer

would need to have on deposit at the qualified clearing agency. 12 Thus, under existing Note H

       99149 (Dec. 13, 2023), 89 FR 2714 (Jan. 16, 2024) (“Treasury Clearing Adopting Release”).
9

       types of transactions in U.S. Treasury securities in customer accounts that have been cleared, settled, and
       novated by the clearing agency are covered by the Item 15 debit: (1) purchases and sales of U.S. Treasury
       securities; and (2) U.S. Treasury securities repurchase and reverse repurchase agreements (together
       “customer position margin”).
10

11

       customers, as is the case under Item 13 and Note F in Rule 15c3-3a for margin required and on deposit with

requirements, a broker-dealer is not permitted to deliver assets belonging to one customer to

meet the margin requirement of another customer, and margin must be calculated and delivered

on a gross basis. 13

                 ii. Delivery of Customer Cash or Securities on Customer-by-Customer Basis

        Another condition, set forth in paragraph (b)(1) of Note H, provides that the customer

position margin must consist of any of the following when delivered by the broker-dealer to meet

a margin requirement resulting from that particular customer’s U.S. Treasury securities positions

that have cleared, settled, and novated at the qualified clearing agency: (i) cash owed to the

customer; or (ii) U.S. Treasury securities or qualified customer securities held in custody by the

broker-dealer for the customer. 14 Paragraph (b)(1) of Note H also permits a broker-dealer to

temporarily prefund a specific customer’s margin requirement, subject to strict limitations.15

                iii. Commission Approval of Qualified Clearing Agency Rules

        The final condition to the application of the Item 15 debit, set out in paragraph (b)(3) of

Note H, requires the Commission to have approved rules of the qualified clearing agency that

meet the conditions of Note H and has published (and not subsequently withdrawn) a notice that

        at 2764-65.
13
        See Treasury Clearing Adopting Release, 89 FR at 2764.
14

15
        See Note H(b)(1)(iii). Specifically, if delivering proprietary U.S. Treasury securities to the qualified
        clearing agency as margin collateral, the broker-dealer must: (1) not use other types of securities collateral
        acceptable to the qualified clearing agency; (2) not owe the customer or hold in custody for the customer
        sufficient cash, U.S. Treasury securities, and/or qualified customer securities to meet a margin requirement

        qualified clearing agency at the time the margin requirement arose; and (3) call for the customer to deliver
        a sufficient amount of cash, U.S. Treasury securities, and/or qualified customer securities to meet the
        margin requirement on the day the margin requirement arose, and must receive a sufficient amount of cash,
        U.S. Treasury securities, and/or qualified customer securities to meet the margin requirement by the close
        of the next business day after the margin requirement arose. See also Treasury Clearing Adopting Release,
        89 FR at 2763.

broker-dealers may include the debit permitted by Note H. 16 At present, the Commission has

published notices approving the rules of three qualified clearing agencies under paragraph (b)(3)

of Note H, and has not subsequently withdrawn any of them. 17

       C.      SIFMA’s Application for Exemptive Relief

       Pursuant to procedures set forth in Rule 240.0-12 of the Exchange Act, the Securities

Industry and Financial Markets Association (“SIFMA”) filed an application for exemptive relief

from section 15(c)(3) of the Exchange Act and Rule 15c3-3a, Note H(b)(1) and (2)(i) thereunder

pursuant to section 36 of the Exchange Act on June 24, 2026. 18 SIFMA requested that the

Commission grant exemptive relief to permit broker-dealers to include an Item 15 debit in their

customer reserve computation in cases where the broker-dealer has delivered the margin

collateral on a net, omnibus basis, rather than on a gross, customer-by-customer basis. 19 The

requested relief would apply to customer accounts at a qualified clearing agency where the

qualified clearing agency calculates customer margin on either a net, omnibus or gross,

customer-by-customer basis that otherwise meets the conditions of Note H (i.e., the conditions

17

       Reserve Computations with Respect to U.S. Treasury Securities, Exchange Act Release No. 34-101729

       15c3-3a, Note H(b)(3) Regarding Application of the Customer Protection Rule Reserve Computations with

       105980.pdf.
19
       See Notice of Application, 91 FR at 48202.

                                                       5

that are not exempted under SIFMA’s proposed request). 20 Further, SIFMA requested that any

exemptive order issued by the Commission provide broker-dealers with the same relief as to their

PAB account holders and PAB reserve computation under Rule 15c3-3a, subject to the same

conditions. 21

        Section 36 of the Exchange Act authorizes the Commission to conditionally or

unconditionally exempt any person, security, or transaction, or any class or classes of persons,

securities, or transactions, from certain provisions of the Exchange Act or certain rules or

regulations thereunder, by rule, regulation, or order, to the extent that such exemption is

necessary or appropriate in the public interest, and is consistent with the protection of investors.

        On July 24, 2026, the Commission issued a Notice of Application seeking comment on

the Application. The Notice of Application was published in the Federal Register on July 30,

2026 to provide interested persons the opportunity to comment. 22 The Commission did not

receive any comments on the Notice of an Application. 23

II.     Discussion of Exemptive Relief

        A. Statement of Relief

        Since the Commission’s adoption of the Treasury Clearing Adopting Release, broker-

dealers undertaking implementation have raised concerns in letters and meetings with

Commission staff about the inefficiencies and costs of the gross basis requirement. 24 For

example, SIFMA stated in its Application that implementing a strict customer-by-customer



20
        See id. at 48203.
21
        See id.
22
        The comment period ended on August 31, 2026. See Notice of Application, 91 FR at 48204.
23
        See Notice of Application [File No. S7-2026-26].
24
        See, e.g., Application, at 2.

                                                       6

condition, discussed below, which conditions this exemptive relief on continued compliance with

the other applicable conditions of Note H not exempted under this order.

       The sixth condition provides that the broker-dealer must adopt and implement written

policies and procedures reasonably designed to ensure ongoing compliance with the conditions

of this exemptive order. This condition will help ensure firms develop the operational and

process controls necessary to ensure that they can comply with the conditions of this order on an

ongoing basis.

       The seventh condition provides that to the extent a broker-dealer delivers margin to a

qualified clearing agency pursuant to this relief, such margin must remain subject to the other

applicable conditions of Note H not exempted under this order, including paragraphs (b)(2)(ii)

through (v). The Commission is adopting this condition to explicitly reflect the limitation on the

scope of the exemptive relief this order provides. Further, this condition is designed to ensure

that broker-dealers comply with the other applicable conditions of Note H not exempted under

this order, which were designed to permit a debit under circumstances that provide protections to

customers.

       The relief is narrowly tailored to what is necessary to permit a broker-dealer to include an

Item 15 debit in the reserve computations without a gross calculation and delivery requirement,

in a manner that is consistent with the customer protection objectives of Rule 15c3-3.

       For the reasons discussed above, providing this exemption is necessary or appropriate in

the public interest, and is consistent with the protection of investors.

III.   Conclusion

       Accordingly, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED, pursuant to section 36(a)(1) of the Exchange

Act, that a broker-dealer is exempt from the requirement in paragraph (b)(2)(i) of Note H of Rule



                                                  15

15c3-3a to deliver the separate margin amount for each customer of the broker-dealer calculated

by the qualified clearing agency on a gross, customer-by-customer basis, as well as the

requirement in paragraph (b)(1) of Note H of Rule 15c3-3a for a broker-dealer to deliver

customer cash or securities to a qualified clearing agency on a gross, customer-by-customer basis

or to temporarily prefund a specific customer’s margin requirement, provided the conditions

below are met. Under this conditional exemption, broker-dealers may include a debit in their

reserve computations for margin required and on deposit with a qualified clearing agency

resulting from transactions in U.S. Treasury securities in customer accounts that have been

cleared, settled, and novated by the clearing agency, in cases where the broker-dealer has

delivered the margin collateral on a net, omnibus basis. This relief applies to customer accounts

at a qualified clearing agency where the qualified clearing agency calculates margin on either a

net, omnibus or gross, customer-by-customer basis, subject to the following conditions:

       (1)     Eligibility Limitation: The relief applies solely to margin required and on deposit

               with a qualified clearing agency in connection with the following types of

               transactions in U.S. Treasury securities in customer accounts that have been

               cleared, settled, and novated by the qualified clearing agency: (1) purchases and

               sales of U.S. Treasury securities; and (2) U.S. Treasury securities repurchase and

               reverse repurchase agreements.

       (2)     The broker-dealer delivers the following cash and securities to the qualified

               clearing agency to meet the customer margin requirement:

               (i)     cash;

               (ii)    U.S. Treasury securities;

               (iii)   qualified customer securities; or



                                                   16

(iv)    any combination of clauses (i) through (iii) above.

(3)   Permitted Debit. The amount the broker-dealer includes in the Item 15 debit in

      the reserve computations must equal the least of:

      (i)     the amount of margin collected from customers in connection with U.S.

              Treasury securities transactions of the broker-dealer’s customers that are

              cleared, settled, and novated by the qualified clearing agency;

      (ii)    the amount of margin required for U.S. Treasury securities positions of the

              broker-dealer’s customers that are cleared, settled, and novated by the

              qualified clearing agency; or

      (iii)   the total of: (A) cash, (B) U.S. Treasury securities, and (C) qualified

              customer securities delivered by the broker-dealer to the qualified clearing

              agency to meet margin requirements arising from U.S. Treasury positions

              of the broker-dealer’s customers that are cleared, settled and novated at the

              qualified clearing agency.

(4)   Documentation: The broker-dealer must maintain books and records sufficient to

      identify the amount of customer margin collected and delivered to the qualified

      clearing agency.

(5)   Qualified Clearing Agency Rulebook Amendments. The rules of the qualified

      clearing agency must have been amended to reflect the conditions of this

      exemptive order.

(6)   Procedures: The broker-dealer must adopt and implement written policies and

      procedures reasonably designed to ensure ongoing compliance with the conditions

      of this exemptive order.



                                        17

(7)     To the extent a broker-dealer delivers margin to a qualified clearing agency

               consistent with this exemptive order, such margin must remain subject to the

               other applicable conditions of Note H not exempted under this order, including

               paragraphs (b)(2)(ii) through (v).



       By the Commission.



Sherry R. Haywood,

Assistant Secretary.

## PDF 1頁

米証券取引委員会（SEC）
公表番号34-106821、案件番号S7-2026-26

中央清算される一部の米国債取引に関し、1934年証券取引所法第36条に基づき、同法第15条(c)(3)および同法規則15c3-3aの注Hからの条件付き適用免除を認める命令

2026年11月4日

### I　序論

#### A　免除命令の概要

証券取引委員会（委員会）は、証券取引所法第36条［1］に基づき、ブローカー・ディーラーに対し、同法規則15c3-3の別表A、第15項の注H（規則15c3-3a注H、以下「注H」）の一部規定からの適用免除を認める。

具体的には、委員会は、証券取引所法第15条(c)(3)［2］および同法に基づく規則15c3-3a注H(b)(1)、(b)(2)(i)の適用からの免除を認める。これによりブローカー・ディーラーは、規則15c3-3aに基づく顧客勘定および他のブローカー・ディーラーの自己証券勘定（PAB）［3］の準備額計算において、適格清算機関［4］によって清算・決済・更改された顧客勘定の米国債取引に伴い要求され、同機関に預託された証拠金を控除項目に含めることができる。［文は次頁へ続く］

［1］15 U.S.C. 78mm。同法第36条(a)(1)は、公共の利益に照らして必要または適切で、投資家保護に合致する範囲で、委員会に対し、規則、規制または命令によって、あらゆる者、証券または取引、あるいはその一つ以上の区分を、条件付きまたは無条件で、同法のいずれの規定からも免除する権限を与える。
［2］15 U.S.C. 78o(c)(3)。
［3］17 CFR 240.15c3-3(a)(16)参照。PABは、ブローカー・ディーラー（外国のブローカー・ディーラーや、その資格で行動する外国銀行を含む）の自己証券勘定のうち、支払いと引渡し、または支払いと受渡しを同時に行う勘定を除くものを指す。口座を管理するブローカー・ディーラーの債権者の請求に劣後する勘定も含まない。
［4］注H(a)参照。「適格清算機関」は、同法第17A条に基づき委員会に登録され、米国債取引の清算、決済および更改を行う清算機関をいう。

紙面1頁

## PDF 2頁

［1頁から続く］清算機関が顧客証拠金を一括口座でネット計算する場合と、顧客ごとにグロス計算する場合のいずれでも、ブローカー・ディーラーが証拠金担保を一括口座でネット差入れしていることを条件とする。［5］

#### B　背景

証券取引所法の規則15c3-3はブローカー・ディーラーの顧客保護規則であり、顧客の現金や証券を保有する業者（顧客資産保管業者）に、経営破綻した場合に顧客へ速やかに返還できるよう、それらの資産を扱うことを求める。このため、同規則は顧客資産保管業者に、顧客の証券・現金を自己の事業活動から分離して保護する二つの主要な措置を求める。第一に、顧客が代金を全額支払った証券と超過証拠金に当たる証券について、現物を保有するか支配を維持する。［6］第二に、顧客準備額計算として規則15c3-3a所定の算式で算出した、顧客に対する現金の純支払債務以上の価額に相当する現金または適格証券（米国債等）を、第三者銀行の口座に準備として保有する。［7］同規則の目的は、業者が財務支援を受けずに秩序ある自主清算を行い、顧客資産を返還できる状態に置くことにある。

2023年12月13日、委員会は証券取引所法に基づき、特定の清算機関に適用される基準を改める規則を採択した。［3頁へ続く］

［5］規則15c3-3別表Aの注H(b)(2)(i)、17 CFR 240.15c3-3a参照。
［6］17 CFR 240.15c3-3(d)参照。
［7］17 CFR 240.15c3-3a（17 CFR 240.15c3-3に基づく業者の顧客・PAB勘定の準備要件を決定する算式）参照。

紙面2頁

## PDF 3頁

［2頁から続く］米国債市場の中央清算機関のリスク管理を強化し、米国債の清算をさらに促進するためである。［8］米国債清算規則の採択文書で、委員会は規則15c3-3aを改め、米国債の中央清算サービスを提供する適格清算機関が要求し、同機関に預託された証拠金を、所定の条件の下で準備額計算における控除に含めることを認めた。［9］

##### i　顧客ポジション証拠金のグロス要件とネット要件

顧客ポジション証拠金を準備額計算の控除に算入する条件には、適格清算機関が採用することを求められる規則に従って証拠金を取り扱うことが含まれる。［10］注H(b)(2)(i)は、適格清算機関が業者の顧客ごとにグロスで証拠金額を算定し、業者が顧客ごとにその額をグロスで差し入れることを求める。［11］委員会は、業者が適格清算機関に預託すべき顧客証拠金の額を算定する際に、ある顧客のポジションのリスクを別の顧客のリスクで相殺できないよう、この要件を採択した。［12］したがって現行注Hの［4頁へ続く］

［8］「米国債の対象清算機関の基準および米国債に関するブローカー・ディーラー顧客保護規則の適用」、公表99149（2023年12月13日）、89 FR 2714（2024年1月16日、以下「米国債清算規則の採択文書」）参照。
［9］同2760～2768頁および規則15c3-3別表Aの注H、17 CFR 240.15c3-3a参照。清算機関が清算・決済・更改した顧客勘定の米国債取引のうち、第15項控除の対象は、米国債の売買と、米国債レポ・リバースレポである（これらの取引の証拠金を「顧客ポジション証拠金」と呼ぶ）。
［10］米国債清算規則の採択文書2764頁および規則15c3-3別表Aの注H(b)(2)、17 CFR 240.15c3-3a参照。
［11］同別表Aの注H(b)(2)(i)、17 CFR 240.15c3-3a参照。
［12］米国債清算規則の採択文書、89 FR 2764頁参照。委員会が検討した代替案、すなわち、業者の全顧客を通算してネット計算し適格清算機関に差し入れた証拠金額に基づく控除を認める要件への変更については、規則15c3-3aの第13項・注Fで扱う［脚注は4頁へ続く］。
